grants.programme: Membership — defamation and legal-threat defence cover
grants.summary: A membership organisation, created by investigative journalists (OCCRP) and lawyers at the Cyrus R. Vance Center, that pools member contributions into a mutual defence fund to cover legal costs of defending public-interest investigative reporting against defamation and other lawfare/SLAPP-style threats. Membership includes pre-publication risk review, response drafting when members receive legal threats, and litigation defence by a specialist media-lawyer network.

amount.note: Membership fee, not a cash grant; reported floor around $1,000 with an average around $3,500 depending on level of legal service, with subsidies available in some cases (figures per third-party press coverage, not directly confirmed on the funder's own page today).

grants.notes: This still checks out as the org's core (only) programme; no separate grant/fund found. Note the working domain is reporters-shield.org (with hyphen) - the source's recorded URL reportersshield.org (no hyphen) may be outdated or a redirect; worth checking. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A free, 24/7 rapid-response service providing real-time technical assistance and cybersecurity advice to civil society groups, activists, media organisations, journalists, bloggers, and human rights defenders facing digital threats. The Helpline aims to respond to all requests within two hours and offers support in ten languages.

amount.note: Provides technical assistance, not a cash grant.

grants.notes: Today's accessnow.org snapshot covered the general 'Access Now Grants' grassroots-grantmaking page and a donor financial log, neither of which detailed the Helpline; details confirmed via web search of the funder's /help/ page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: ARIJ — Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism
grants.summary: ARIJ awards grants of US$2,500 to Arab journalists to produce digital, audio, or televised investigative reports exposing environmental, legal, and financial corruption, separately covering filming and editing expenses. ARIJ's own site nav invites ongoing submission of investigation proposals alongside editorial mentoring and fact-checking support.

amount.note: US$2,500 per investigative report grant; ARIJ separately covers filming/video-editing expenses.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of arij.net confirms a standing 'Submit an investigation' (قدم تحقيقاً) intake and references pausing responses over winter holidays, indicating an ongoing/rolling submission process, but did not capture ARIJ's dedicated grants page. The $2,500 amount and eligible-country list come from a search of ARIJ's own site (en.arij.net) rather than today's snapshot content. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A year-long, non-residential fellowship for activists, investigative journalists, filmmakers and lawyers to collaboratively investigate one pressing social-justice issue chosen around an annual theme. Reported support has included a fellow stipend, project funding, and a 'connect fund' for collaboration, plus training, mentorship and networking.

amount.note: Previously reported (secondary sources, prior cycle): fellow stipend up to US$64,900, project funding up to US$10,000, and a connect fund up to US$5,000.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot confirms the programme exists ('Fellowships for Activists, Investigative Journalists, Filmmakers and Lawyers to spend a year working on one pressing social justice challenge') and states verbatim: BERTHA FOUNDATION DOES NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS — applications are only taken during announced windows. The most recent verified deadline (28 Jul 2025, for a fellowship year beginning Jan 2026) has passed; no 2026/2027 call was found open today. Programme appears to recur roughly annually. Not confirmed on the funder's own page for deadline/amount specifics.

grants.programme: The Gene Roberts Fund for Emergency Assistance
grants.summary: CPJ provides case-by-case emergency financial support to journalists who have recently faced a serious incident and whose safety is compromised, through the Gene Roberts Fund, administered by CPJ staff in New York and overseen by a board committee. Funds may cover relocation expenses, medical costs, mental health support, legal help and other urgent needs; CPJ cannot fund visa or immigration/asylum applications, education, or general medical needs unrelated to an act of journalism. CPJ separately offers non-financial assistance such as referrals to partner organisations, fellowship/residency information, and safety or trauma consultations.

amount.note: Described only as 'modest grants' assessed case by case; no fixed amount stated on CPJ's own pages.

grants.notes: CPJ explicitly excludes visa applications, immigration/asylum claims, education costs, and general medical needs unrelated to an act of journalism from this fund's scope.

grants.summary: Craig Newmark Philanthropies accepts funding proposals from registered nonprofits on a rolling basis across its focus areas, one of which is 'Promoting the Truth'; a separate portal exists only for veterans/military-family support. Applicants must supply proof of active 501(c)(3)/public-charity status with the IRS and Secretary of State, and CNP says it cannot review or fund every request. Multi-year commitments are released annually based on progress and the effectiveness of the grantee's communication and collaboration.

amount.note: Application asks for a 'grant amount requested' but no published range.

grants.notes: Reporting from January 2026 (Nieman Journalism Lab) quotes founder Craig Newmark saying he is pulling back from journalism funding because 'a lot of my efforts haven't been as effective as I'd like them to be,' now treating journalism as a secondary focus behind cybersecurity and safety of journalists — so openness to new 'Promoting the Truth' proposals from newsrooms may be more limited than the site's generic apply page suggests. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Media Defence provides legal grants and practical support for the defence of journalists, citizen journalists and media outlets facing prosecution or civil suits connected to their work. Applications for case support are usually made by the lawyer handling the case but can also be made by the journalist, their family or friends, or a relevant support organisation. Media Defence combines financial assistance with practical support to organisations that have, or wish to establish, a legal aid unit for journalists.

amount.note: Covers legal costs case-by-case; no published amount range found.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for mediadefence.org (fetch never produced a file), so this entry is built from web search of the funder's own site pages (apply-for-case-support/, get-help/). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Partner support for legal aid organisations
grants.summary: Media Defence funds and supports partner organisations that operate, or want to establish, a legal aid unit providing free legal support to journalists, citizen journalists and media outlets facing legal threats. In 2025 it reported awarding over £350,000 in grants to 19 partner organisations running media-defence centres across Europe, Latin America, Africa, Asia, and the Middle East/North Africa, enabling litigation of hundreds of freedom-of-expression cases.

amount.note: £350,000+ distributed across 19 partner organisations in 2025 in aggregate; no per-grant figure published.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for mediadefence.org; this entry (distinct from individual case support) is built from web search covering the funder's own 'get-help' page and a 2025 partner impact report. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: RSF's Assistance Desk provides financial and administrative help to professional and citizen journalists who have been the target of reprisals connected to their reporting, covering emergency relocation, legal fees, medical costs, psychological support and replacement of destroyed or confiscated equipment. Grants generally range from EUR 500 to EUR 2,500 per case, and RSF may also support applications for international protection or asylum where its research supports it. In 2025 RSF reported aiding nearly 750 journalists in 76 countries.

amount.note: Per-case emergency support grant range reported by RSF; larger relocation/asylum cases may exceed this via other mechanisms.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for rsf.org/en/assistance; amount range and scope are drawn from web search of RSF's own reporting and individual-support page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: RSF launched a grant programme reimbursing US-based journalists for personal protective equipment, including first-aid kits, helmets, eye protection, protective vests and respirator masks, in response to escalating on-the-ground risks to reporters covering protests and conflict.

amount.note: Reimbursement scheme; no published cap found.

grants.notes: No snapshot was available for this source; found via web search of RSF's own news release announcing the US-specific PRESS equipment grant programme. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Balkan Trust for Democracy (German Marshall Fund)
grants.programme: BTD Support for Western Balkans 6 — Media Freedom track
grants.summary: The Balkan Trust for Democracy funds civil society organisations registered in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. One of its two current thematic tracks is strengthening media freedom (the other combats domestic and gender-based violence), delivered as a sub-granting scheme realised with the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Royal Norwegian Embassy in Belgrade. Proposals have previously been accepted on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline until the grantmaking budget is exhausted.
grants.notes: Re-checked on 2026-09-18: today's snapshot of gmfus.org again only captured generic GMF organisational pages (About, Global Power Shifts, Fellowships, donor FAQ, a press article) and never reached Balkan Trust for Democracy's own grant-call pages, so this entry is still built from a web search of GMF's own site (balkan-trust-democracy/support-western-balkans-6 and the related WB6 media-freedom announcement page confirm the six-country scope and Norwegian co-funding). Only registered civil-society organisations in the six WB6 countries may apply — not individual freelancers. No corroborated deadline was found; secondary sites reference other, separate WB6 media programmes (e.g. EU/EEAS 'WB6 MEDIA') with their own deadlines that should not be conflated with this BTD call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Reporters Respond is an emergency response fund, active since 2011, that provides direct assistance, legal support and safety advice to journalists and media organisations worldwide facing (online) harassment, intimidation, legal proceedings or violence because of their work, helping them resume their work as quickly as possible. In the most urgent cases the fund states it can offer support within 24 hours.

amount.note: Assessed case by case; the funder's own page states support can be offered within 24 hours in the most urgent cases.

grants.notes: Confirmed today verbatim on Free Press Unlimited's own page (fetched as page 2 of the free-press-unlimited source's snapshot, which links directly to this page): 'active since 2011 ... enabling them to resume their work as quickly as possible ... worldwide ... In the most urgent cases, support can be offered within 24 hours.' Contact given: reportersrespond@freepressunlimited.org. Additional eligibility detail from prior verification (2026-09-18, via search, not reconfirmed today): situation must be corroborated by at least two trusted sources independent of the applicant; application form accepts English, French, Spanish and Portuguese.

grants.programme: Healthy Information Sphere (International Human Rights Programme)
grants.summary: Oak Foundation's Healthy Information Sphere portfolio, within its International Human Rights Programme, supports independent journalism, media pluralism, digital rights and information integrity work aimed at holding power to account. Not-for-profit organisations not already invited by a programme officer may submit an unsolicited Letter of Enquiry, though the Foundation states it has no open call for proposals and funds only a small share of the enquiries it receives.

amount.note: Not stated publicly; programme budgets are reported to be allocated roughly a year in advance and only a small number of unsolicited enquiries are funded each year.

grants.notes: This is a general unsolicited-Letter-of-Enquiry intake, not a journalism-specific open call; the Foundation explicitly says it has no open call for proposals at this time and only responds to enquiries submitted via its online form. Geographic focus reported as EU, US, UK, Brazil and other 'global East' geographies, so global scope is uncertain. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: MDIF provides loans, equity investments, loan guarantees and related business advisory support to independent media and information businesses operating in countries with a history of media oppression, ownership concentration, a state of democratic transition, or information poverty. This is investment capital rather than grant funding; applicants must be independent of government or other interest groups, complete an inquiry form, and go through a multi-step due-diligence process that typically takes several months.

amount.note: Case by case; specific loan/equity size ranges not stated publicly. MDIF reports a portfolio of roughly $118.7M across around 58-60 media businesses in 31-34 countries as of its most recent reporting found.

grants.notes: Replaces prior unverified seed entry. Not a grant — financing carries repayment (debt) or ownership (equity) terms. No snapshot of the funder's page was available this run, so this is based on web search results only. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: GNI Lab is a 12-week program combining virtual sessions, practical exercises and personalized mentoring that helps independent news creators and small digital media outlets strengthen their journalism using Google tools, audience-building practices, and revenue-diversification strategies. It is run by SembraMedia in partnership with the Google News Initiative for participants from Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru and Uruguay. The 2026 cohort's application window closed on August 2, 2026.

amount.note: Training and mentoring program; no cash grant amount was stated in search results.

grants.notes: The 2026 cohort's application window closed August 2, 2026 (Argentina time). SembraMedia runs this as a recurring initiative, so a future cycle is likely, but no confirmed next call date was found in search results. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: PULSE, n-ost's cross-border journalism network ('Europe beyond the beat'), funds small reporting teams of two journalists from different eligible countries to produce collaborative stories under one of four Thematic Networks (media and society, media/AI legislation, digitalisation, and disinformation/fact-checking). The 2026 call was open to journalists with fiscal residency across a broad list of countries including EU and EU-candidate states, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Brazil, China, India, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Russia, the UK, the US, Uzbekistan, Belarus, Israel/Palestine and Iran, with two teams funded per network. The pitch deadline was extended to July 20, 2026, with results expected in September 2026, so this cycle is now closed to new applicants.

amount.note: Grant amount per team was not stated in search results.

grants.notes: The 2026 Thematic Network pitch deadline (extended to July 20, 2026) has passed and results were due in September 2026. PULSE runs as a recurring annual programme, so a future call is expected, but no next date was found. The 2026 call's eligible journalist countries extend well beyond Europe (e.g. Brazil, China, India, US) even though the programme is Europe-focused; geoScope here reflects the programme's Europe focus, not the full eligibility list. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Media Forward Fund — General Funding Line
grants.summary: A recurring funding line (calls roughly twice a year, in February and September) offering up to EUR 400,000 per application over two years to media organisations in the DACH region (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) developing new business models and revenue sources to sustain public-interest journalism.

amount.note: Up to €400,000 per application over two years.

grants.notes: The erste-stiftung snapshot did not surface this programme page (it only captured the homepage and the unrelated Facing the Future Fellowship); all details here are from Media Forward Fund's and ERSTE Foundation's own sites found via web search, which confirms a new call opened 7 September 2026 but does not state a precise submission deadline for this call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Grants of EUR 25,000–35,000, covering up to 100% of costs (incl. 15% overheads) for up to 18 months, for projects involving organisations from at least 3 V4 countries (or 2 neighbouring V4 countries for cross-border projects). Supported areas include anti-corruption work with investigative journalists and watchdogs, and improving media/information literacy and resilience to disinformation.

amount.note: Covers up to 100% of costs including 15% overheads; project duration up to 18 months.

grants.notes: No snapshot exists for visegrad-fund; all facts sourced via web search of the Fund's own site (deadlines recur three times a year: 1 Feb, 1 Jun, 1 Oct). Journalism/media projects are one of several eligible themes, not the fund's sole purpose. Not confirmed on the funder's own page. Replaces the prior unverified 'seed' placeholder entry (previously id visegrad-fund-grants) and supersedes an aggregator-sourced duplicate previously listed under gfmd-fundings, per the funder's-own-source preference rule.

grants.programme: African Academy for Open Source Investigation (AAOSI) Fellowship
grants.summary: Stipend-based fellowships pairing journalists and civil-society researchers with veteran forensic analysts to learn open-source and social-media intelligence (OSINT/SOCMINT) investigation techniques over about four months. Rounds rotate through different African sub-regions (Sahel/West/East Africa in a February 2026 round; Southern Africa in a mid-2026 round), each with its own call and deadline.

amount.note: Described as stipend-based; specific amount not stated in available sources.

grants.notes: Recurring fellowship with multiple regional rounds per year; the Southern Africa round's 10 August 2026 deadline has passed, and an earlier round covering the Sahel, West Africa and East Africa closed in early 2026. Six fellowships per round, roughly four months. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Six stipend-based, six-month fellowships run by Code for Africa's African Fact-Checking Alliance (AFCA) for journalists and fact-checkers in Southern Africa, with editorial training and mentoring from CfA's PesaCheck, iLAB and AFCA teams to produce fact-checking work on regional mis/disinformation.

amount.note: Stipend-based; specific amount not stated in available sources.

grants.notes: 2026 round's eligibility was limited to Angola, Botswana, Comoros, DRC, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe; deadline of 10 April 2026 has passed. Recurring annual programme, six-month fellowship term. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism
grants.programme: Report Women! Female Reporters Leadership Programme (FRLP) Fellowship
grants.summary: An annual fellowship for mid-career female investigative journalists in Nigeria, combining residential training on leadership and investigative reporting with six months of mentorship to produce investigative stories and leadership projects addressing gender gaps in newsrooms. Funded via the Report Women! project with Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation support.

amount.note: Financial stipend not stated; support described as residential training plus six months of mentorship.

grants.notes: Sixth cohort's deadline was 18 February 2025; requires at least four years of post-NYSC experience and current or emerging leadership role. No 2026/2027 cohort dates were found, so deadline is left null pending confirmation. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism
grants.programme: CMEDIA Story Support: Strengthening Local Accountability
grants.summary: Under the Collaborative Media Engagement for Development, Inclusivity, and Accountability (CMEDIA) project, WSCIJ invites investigative story pitches from Nigerian journalists on subnational (state and local) government issues such as health, education, infrastructure, water, housing and disability. Selected journalists research, write and publish the resulting stories. Funded by the MacArthur Foundation.

amount.note: Amount not stated in available sources.

grants.notes: Call was posted around mid-April 2026; no explicit deadline was found, so it is marked closed as a conservative estimate given the elapsed time, but this should be reconfirmed. Part of the recurring CMEDIA project. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Ten scholarships of up to USD 2,100 each to support an investigative journalism project reported through a solutions-journalism lens. Past editions have focused on specific Central American countries (El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua); the programme runs in successive regional editions.

amount.note: Up to USD 2,100 per fellow; 10 fellowships awarded per edition.

grants.notes: Runs as successive regional editions (e.g. 'Triángulo Norte y Nicaragua'); exact current-edition deadline could not be confirmed, so left null. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Fundación Gabo's flagship annual scholarship programme funds journalism projects by journalists across Latin America, with 25 scholarships ranging from USD 2,500 to USD 8,000 awarded per cycle.

amount.note: 25 scholarships awarded per cycle, amounts ranging between the stated min and max.

grants.notes: One source described this cycle's application window as closing around 1 July, which (if referring to 2026) has already passed; the exact year could not be confirmed on the funder's own page, so the deadline field is left null. Open to journalists from any Latin American country. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Grants co-run with partner foundations (e.g. Fundación Avina, Habitat for Humanity) supporting investigative journalism on sustainable-development themes in Latin America, such as inclusive recycling. Winners receive a cash stipend plus access to editorial mentorship.

amount.note: USD 800 stipend cited for the 'Edición Hábitat' round; amount varies by themed edition.

grants.notes: Runs as a series of themed editions with different co-funders and topics (recycling, habitat, etc.); no current-edition deadline was confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas
grants.summary: JNI's general grants programme funds journalists and media organisations to produce public-interest journalism, with a particular focus on Australian reporting and on Asia. Freelancers are advised to apply with the backing of a media platform.

amount.note: Amount not stated.

grants.notes: News coverage from 2026 indicates JNI adopted a revised strategy under which it will no longer award grants to major news organisations, following organisational turbulence; scope and current status of smaller/individual grants could not be confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas (with the Walkley Foundation)
grants.summary: A grant administered with the Walkley Foundation to help Australian and permanent-resident freelance journalists produce a significant body of work, in any medium, reporting on Asia.

amount.note: Up to $25,000 cited; currency not explicitly stated in the source (the programme is Australian-run).

grants.notes: Restricted to Australian citizens/permanent residents. No 2026 application round could be confirmed; the most recent detailed information found dated to 2020, and JNI's 2026 strategy shift (see JNI Grants entry) may affect this programme's status. Marked closed pending confirmation of an active round. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A prototyping micro-grant fund helping news and media entrepreneurs in Asia ideate, launch, test and iterate news products and services. Splice does not take an equity stake in the ventures it supports.

amount.note: Described as micro-grants / pre-seed, non-equity funding; specific amount not stated.

grants.notes: For media startups/entrepreneurs building new news products, rather than individual freelance journalists. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: The sixth yearly Creative Europe cross-sectoral call funding transnational consortia of news media organisations on cross-border collaboration, sustainable business models and journalistic projects, including strand topics for economic resilience ('Collaborations') and support for media of particular democratic relevance such as local, community and investigative outlets ('Pluralism').

amount.note: Total call budget €13,800,000; maximum grant per project €2,000,000; co-financing rate up to 80% of eligible costs.

grants.notes: Requires a consortium of at least 3 independent entities from 3 different eligible countries; projects run 24 months, expected to start late 2026. Eligible countries include EU member states, EEA/associated countries, plus Georgia and Ukraine. This 2026 round's deadline (4 Feb 2026) has passed; it is an annually recurring call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A Creative Europe cross-sectoral call funding innovative, cross-border media-literacy projects, open to consortia including media organisations, educational institutions and other bodies working to build public resilience against disinformation.

amount.note: Total indicative budget €3,000,000 for 2026; maximum grant per project €500,000; co-financing rate up to 70% of eligible costs.

grants.notes: Requires a consortium of at least 3 entities from 3 different Creative Europe-participating countries; projects run up to 2 years. Also open to Georgia and Ukraine. This round's deadline (11 March 2026) has passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Nieman Foundation for Journalism, Harvard University
grants.summary: A fully funded academic-year fellowship for non-U.S. working journalists (including those working in the U.S.) to study at Harvard University, audit classes, and take part in Nieman seminars and events. Fellows receive a living stipend plus child care and health insurance allowances and must refrain from professional work during the fellowship year.

amount.note: $87,500 stipend paid over a nine-month period to cover living costs; additional child care allowance (up to $16,750/year for 4+ children) and health insurance supplement (up to $6,250) also available, per the funder's Stipend & Allowances page.

grants.notes: Recurring annual deadline of December 1 stated on the funder's page for the International Nieman Fellowship (exact year not stated verbatim, so left as recurring rather than a fixed date). Nine-month academic-year fellowship, fellow relocates to Cambridge, MA. Requires 5+ years of full-time media experience (freelancers explicitly eligible); no PR/corporate-comms work; must speak/read/write English fluently; must not have done a residential fellowship of 4+ months in the prior 5 years. Must reside in Cambridge, MA during the fellowship and refrain from paid professional work except as approved. A designated Nieman-Berkman Klein Fellowship in Journalism Innovation track exists within the same application. Visa note: applicants from countries where the U.S. has suspended nonimmigrant (J) visas are advised to wait unless they hold another eligible citizenship.

grants.funder: Nieman Foundation for Journalism, Harvard University
grants.summary: A fully funded academic-year fellowship for U.S.-citizen working journalists (including those working outside the U.S.) to study at Harvard University, audit classes, and take part in Nieman seminars and events. Fellows receive a living stipend plus child care and health insurance allowances and must refrain from professional work during the fellowship year.

amount.note: $87,500 stipend paid over a nine-month period to cover living costs; additional child care allowance (up to $16,750/year for 4+ children) and health insurance supplement (up to $6,250) also available, per the funder's Stipend & Allowances page.

grants.notes: Recurring annual deadline of January 31 stated on the funder's page for the U.S. Nieman Fellowship (exact year not stated verbatim, so left as recurring rather than a fixed date). Nine-month academic-year fellowship, fellow relocates to Cambridge, MA. Same eligibility rules as the international track: 5+ years full-time media experience, freelancers explicitly eligible, no PR/corporate-comms work, English fluency required.

grants.funder: John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships, Stanford University
grants.summary: A nine-month residential fellowship at Stanford University for up to 20 journalists per year from around the world to work collaboratively on journalism's most urgent challenges, with personalized mentorship and access to Stanford classes. The 2026-27 class received a stipend of $130,000 plus Stanford health insurance for fellows, spouses, and children, and included both newsroom staff, freelancers, and people supporting journalism organisations.

amount.note: $130,000 stipend and Stanford health insurance for fellows, spouses and children, as stated for the 2026-27 (Class of 2027) cohort; figure not explicitly guaranteed to repeat for future cycles on the fetched page.

grants.notes: Nine-month residential fellowship in Stanford, California; fellow relocates for the term. The fetched homepage and news pages did not state an application deadline or opening date for the next cycle; see the funder's Application FAQ page for current dates. Up to 20 fellows/year; the 2026-27 class (13 fellows) included 8 U.S. and 5 international fellows, drawn from news organisations, freelancers, and organisations supporting journalists. Fellows have a personal coach (director) throughout the year; partners ('affiliates') are welcome at most gatherings.

grants.funder: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
grants.summary: A programme for practising, mid-career journalists and editors to spend three or six months in Oxford researching a personal project, with most fellows fully funded (fees, monthly stipend, travel and visa costs covered). Fellowships begin in October, January or April and require a minimum of five years' journalistic experience; freelancers may apply but those in PR/corporate communications may not.

amount.note: Most fellows are fully funded: fees covered plus a monthly stipend of £2,000 to cover accommodation, food and general living expenses, with travel to/from the UK and visa costs also covered. Some fellows instead come via sponsoring organisations with their own funding and selection process (e.g. Thomson Reuters Foundation Fellowship, Mona Megalli Fellowship for a Middle East journalist).

grants.notes: As of the fetched pages (18 Sep 2026), applications for fellowships beginning in the 2026-27 academic year are stated as closed on two separate fetched pages, with the programme reopening in January 2027 for cohorts starting October 2026, January 2027 or April 2027; exact reopening date not stated. One page fragment inconsistently also read 'applications are now open' — likely stale cached content — so this was not relied on for status. Fellowship lasts three or six months in Oxford, UK; fellow relocates for the term. Requires 5+ years' journalistic experience; open to journalists worldwide; not open to PR/public affairs/corporate communications staff; fellows must plan to return to journalism afterward.

grants.funder: Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan
grants.summary: An eight-month residential fellowship (late August through April) at the University of Michigan for journalists with at least five years of experience, including freelancers, to pursue a self-directed course of study. The programme includes a living stipend, relocation allowance, health insurance, and University of Michigan course auditing, with typically up to six international fellows joining ten to twelve U.S. journalists each year.

amount.note: Reported as an $85,000 stipend disbursed monthly August through April, plus a $5,000 relocation allowance and health insurance coverage. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: No snapshot available for this source; sourced via WebSearch of secondary pages referencing wallacehouse.umich.edu content, not the funder's own page directly. Eight-month residential fellowship, Ann Arbor, Michigan; fellow relocates for the term. International applications for the 2026-27 cohort are described as closed, with applications for 2027-28 said to open in October 2026 (exact date not given). Up to six international fellows typically join ten to twelve U.S. journalists; international finalists are interviewed in January/February to allow time for visa processing. Requires 5+ years of journalism experience. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A three-month fellowship at the IWM in Vienna giving European journalists time off from their regular duties to pursue in-depth, independent research on a topic of their choice. Fellows receive a monthly stipend plus office space and access to the IWM academic community.

amount.note: Monthly stipend for the 3-month term.

grants.notes: Term runs three consecutive months, placement at the IWM in Vienna, between September 2026 and June 2027 for the cohort tied to this deadline. Open to European journalists (including Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Turkey) with several years' professional experience in print, broadcast or online journalism; no explicit language requirement stated. The 16 January 2026 deadline for this cycle has passed; the call recurs annually but the next deadline is not yet confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Grants and Investments — Storytelling grants (Explorer Level I/II)
grants.summary: National Geographic Society's Explorer grants fund project leaders in conservation, education, research, storytelling and technology; the storytelling category explicitly covers journalism, photography, filmmaking and digital media. The Society has moved to a request-for-proposals model with themed windows rather than a standing rolling call.

amount.note: Level I grants up to $20,000; Level II grants up to $100,000 for established applicants pushing for significant impact.

grants.notes: Applicants must be 18+; those working outside their home country must include a local collaborator. The Society's own page currently lists no open opportunities and states a storytelling-related application window opens 1 October 2026; specific deadline and amount for that window were not stated in available evidence. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: National Geographic Society (with The Climate Pledge)
grants.programme: National Geographic Society × The Climate Pledge Storytelling Grant
grants.summary: A partnership between the National Geographic Society and The Climate Pledge funding storytelling projects on climate resilience, energy transition and sustainability solutions. Open to professional storytellers, journalists, documentary filmmakers, photographers, writers and podcast producers worldwide, whether or not they have previously held National Geographic Explorer status.

amount.note: Up to $100,000; early-career applicants (5 years or less experience) advised to request no more than $20,000. Project implementation period up to 2 years.

grants.notes: 2026 cycle deadline was 25 May 2026, 11:59pm EDT; applications submitted in English via NatGeo's online portal. Covers climate & energy transition, nature & land systems, and human & built systems topics. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Heinrich Böll Stiftung (Washington, DC / North America Office)
grants.summary: Supports journalists based in the US, Canada or Germany (and, for Global South-focused stories, journalists in Africa, Asia and Latin America) to research and report transatlantic stories on climate & energy, democracy, foreign & security, technology, or global development policy. Fellows choose either an on-the-ground track including travel or a remote/digital track.

amount.note: Reported as $2,000 for the digital/remote track (no travel) and $4,000 for the on-the-ground track (with travel); figures not verified on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: Run out of the Heinrich Böll Stiftung's Washington, DC office rather than the German headquarters site. Secondary sources give conflicting application-deadline dates (13 March vs 24 March) and fellows are expected to submit a first draft by 1 October and publish by year-end, meaning the 2026 cohort's window has already closed as of this check. Exact current-cycle deadline and amount could not be confirmed on the funder's own page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung — Media Programme South East Europe
grants.summary: A scholarship for Bachelor's students (from their 2nd academic year) and Master's students of any major who are already actively engaged at a media outlet, at universities across South-East Europe. Scholars receive a monthly grant and access to exchanges with regional and international media experts.

amount.note: Monthly grant amount not stated in the pages reviewed.

grants.notes: Applicants must show a distinctive interest in social/political issues and alignment with KAS's values (democracy, freedom, rule of law, pluralism, European unification). Universities in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania and Serbia are covered. Most recently reported call closed 10 June 2025; recurs each academic year/semester but the 2026 deadline could not be confirmed on the funder's own page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Adenauer Fellowship for Media and Communication
grants.summary: Supports young journalists from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and the Philippines (with related country-specific tracks also open to journalists in Indonesia and Malaysia) to pursue a Master's degree in journalism, combining a semester grant, tuition support and study-related travel costs.

amount.note: Semester grant of EUR 500 plus tuition fees up to EUR 6,000, plus study-related travel costs.

grants.notes: Applicants must be 35 or under at the start of postgraduate study, have at least 2 years' relevant work experience, and be fluent in English at C1 level or above. Details were assembled from multiple secondary scholarship-database listings that may conflate slightly different regional tracks; a related 2026 call for Indonesia/Malaysia journalists had a stated deadline of 31 March 2026, already passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Brings two journalists a year from countries with restricted press and information freedoms to Berlin for a six-month stay focused on rest, protection and recovery, for example after reporting from conflict zones or under state-security pressure. Run annually since 2015, and since 2026 organised independently by the taz Panter Stiftung in cooperation with Reporters Without Borders.

amount.note: Travel costs reimbursed, Berlin accommodation organised, pocket money provided, and free local public transport for up to 3 months; no stipend figure stated.

grants.notes: Six-month Berlin stay (reported as May–October 2026 for this cohort) for two journalists worldwide from countries with restricted press/information freedoms; no language or minimum-experience requirement stated. This cohort's application window (15 Dec 2025 – 15 Jan 2026) has closed; recurs annually. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Sends around ten journalists working in Germany on a group study trip to Washington D.C., Philadelphia and New York to examine the US media landscape, followed by a period of independent research. Applicants submit a CV and a short English-language motivation letter describing their research project.

amount.note: Covers travel, accommodation and programme costs for the 12-day group trip, and partially covers costs for the following 9-day period of independent research.

grants.notes: Open to journalists working in Germany with sufficient English; age and nationality are not restricted. 2026 trip runs September/October 2026; the informal-application deadline (8 March 2026) has passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Funds two 18-month traineeships per year in the taz newsroom for aspiring journalists with diverse backgrounds who lack classical journalism training or credentials, explicitly welcoming applicants who face discrimination based on origin, religion, gender, gender identity or disability.

amount.note: Each traineeship reportedly costs the foundation approximately EUR 25,000 (donation-funded); this funds the placement rather than being a grant paid directly to the applicant.

grants.notes: 18-month in-house traineeship at taz rotating through newsroom departments; no formal degree or certificate required. 2026 intake (deadline 18 Feb 2026, start June 2026) has already begun; recurs annually. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic
grants.programme: Transition Promotion Programme (TRANS) — Local Transition Projects
grants.summary: TRANS is the Czech MFA's framework for supporting human rights, democracy and civil-society development abroad. Local Transition Projects (LTPs) are run individually by Czech embassies and can fund work on rule of law, civic participation, and freedom of expression and information — including freedom of the media — implemented by non-governmental organisations.
grants.eligibleActivity: TRANS's own stated thematic pillars include 'promoting the freedom of expression and information, including the freedom of the media', alongside civil-society support, political participation and rule-of-law themes with no media component — so a newsroom or media NGO could apply for an LTP under that specific pillar, but the programme is not media-exclusive.

amount.note: A CZK 500,000 per-project ceiling for the most recently reported cycle comes from secondary/embassy sources, not from the MFA's own page as captured.

grants.notes: The programme is decentralised: each Czech embassy runs its own LTP call with its own budget, exact themes and deadline. The MFA's own page (captured today, only 268 words) just points to 'an overview of current grant calls' rather than listing terms itself. Reported cycle details (CZK 500,000 ceiling, 8 Dec 2025 deadline for a Mar-Oct 2026 project window, NGO-only implementer, four thematic pillars including media freedom) come from secondary aggregators and individual embassy call pages, not the MFA page captured today; that round's deadline has already passed and no newer cycle is visible on the captured page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A Dutch government fund supporting civil-society human rights work worldwide, disbursed mainly through periodic country-specific calls run by individual Dutch embassies. Priority themes include preventing attacks on and obstacles to journalists and media workers, and the long-term sustainability of independent media outlets, alongside other human-rights themes (e.g. LGBTIQ+ equality, freedom of religion).
grants.eligibleActivity: This is a broad human-rights fund, not media-exclusive, but journalist safety and independent-media sustainability are named as stated priority themes within it, so a media organisation could apply under those specific themes via the relevant embassy's call.

amount.note: Amount varies by embassy/country call; no figure found.

grants.notes: Funding is administered per-country through individual Dutch embassies/consulates, each running its own call with its own deadline (e.g. a Hungary-specific 2026 call had a 1 March 2026 deadline, already passed); there is no single global deadline or application portal. Interested applicants should check their nearest Dutch embassy's page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Rapid-response emergency funding of up to €10,000 for human rights defenders, journalists, activists and organisations facing an active digital threat or attack, covering costs that directly reduce the risk or impact of that attack over a period of up to four months. Digital Defenders Partnership aims to respond to eligible requests within two weeks.

amount.note: Up to €10,000; covers activities for a maximum of four months.

grants.notes: Journalists are explicitly named as eligible applicants alongside human rights defenders, activists and organisations facing digital threats/attacks. Apply via an eligibility check on the funder's site or by emailing team@digitaldefenders.org. Digital Defenders Partnership's other funds (Regional Partnership Fund, Community and Network Fund) appear aimed at civil-society organisations generally rather than journalists specifically, so were not recorded. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Google News Initiative (via JournalismAI / Polis, LSE)
grants.summary: A GNI-supported programme funding news publishers to build and integrate AI-powered prototypes into newsroom workflows over an approximately nine-month programme, with mentoring alongside the funding. The most recent (second) cohort supported 12 publishers from 11 countries with grants reported at $50,000 or $100,000 each, running from around February 2026.

amount.note: Reported grant sizes for the 2025-2026 cohort; not directly confirmed on the funder's own page today.

grants.notes: This is a competitive but genuinely fund-for-future-work programme (selected publishers get grants + mentoring to build prototypes), not a prize for past work, so it was recorded despite the 'challenge' name. The most recent round's application deadline (3 Dec 2025) has passed and the next round's dates were not found. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: An annual programme for established U.S. news organisations with a proven business model and a credible plan to expand into a new market, providing roughly $100,000 in grant funding alongside a year of business coaching (delivered via Blue Engine Collaborative) to support the expansion.

amount.note: Reported as roughly $100,000 per selected publisher, plus a year of coaching; not directly confirmed on the funder's own page today.

grants.notes: US-only (not global) despite the source's declared global scope - eligibility is restricted to U.S.-based news organisations. The 2026 round's deadline (7 May 2026) has passed; the programme runs annually, so a new round is expected but dates were not found. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program (Fulbright / J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board, U.S. Department of State)
grants.summary: A non-degree fellowship bringing accomplished, mid-career professionals from designated countries to a US host university for 10 months of graduate-level coursework, professional development and mentoring, with Communications/Journalism (including investigative and broadcast journalism, digital media and public relations) as one of the designated fields. Applications are submitted through the applicant's home-country U.S. Embassy, each on its own country-specific deadline.

amount.note: No dollar figure confirmed today; program is reported to cover tuition and university fees, a monthly maintenance allowance, a book/supplies allowance, a computer subsidy, round-trip international travel to the host institution (and to English-language training if required), domestic travel to a Washington, D.C. seminar, and supplementary funds for professional activities such as field trips/conferences. Funding does not extend to dependents/family members.

grants.notes: Duration: 10 months, hosted at a US university (specific placement varies by fellow). Deadlines are set per-country by the local U.S. Embassy - for the 2027-2028 cohort these fell between roughly late June and late August 2026, all already passed as of today. The next cycle (2028-2029) is reported to open for applications around May 2027, per third-party embassy/press pages, not the funder's own site. Eligibility generally requires several years of professional experience and English proficiency (exact thresholds not directly confirmed today). Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A nine-month residential fellowship in Cambridge, Massachusetts for 10 science journalists worldwide to deepen expertise in a science, health, technology or environmental specialty while auditing MIT and Harvard courses. Open to full-time staff or freelance journalists with at least three years of science/health/tech/environment reporting experience.

amount.note: Stipend of $85,000 disbursed over 9.5 months, plus additional support for travel, housing and basic health insurance for fellows and their families.

grants.notes: The 2026-2027 cycle opened 15 Nov 2025 and closed 9 Jan 2026 (already passed); those fellows are currently in residence. Applicants must not have completed a fellowship of four months or longer in the two years prior. No snapshot was fetched for this source today; details sourced via web search of secondary listings referencing the funder's own Submittable page. Next cycle (2027-2028) likely opens around November 2026, based on the annual pattern, but no confirmed date yet. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

amount.note: Amount not stated in evidence reviewed.

grants.summary: A year-long fellowship for journalists of color combining monthly virtual skills-building sessions, D.C.-based training and mentor matches with veteran journalists, aimed at supporting retention and advancement in U.S. newsrooms.

grants.summary: About ten named funds that cover travel, registration and membership costs for journalists to attend IRE's conferences (the IRE Conference, NICAR and AccessFest), each with its own eligibility rules — some restricted to U.S. journalists, students, TV reporters, or specific beats such as immigration or rural news.

amount.note: Typically covers IRE membership (up to $75), conference registration, and for several funds four hotel nights (roughly $932-$1,100) plus a travel stipend ($500-$650); these are travel/attendance grants, not cash awards.

Sager, Godfrey Wells Stancill, Sandra Thomas Environmental, Susan Carroll, Apples & Oranges, Diversity, Napoli Management Group TV, Jennifer Leonard, James Richard Bennett, David Donald and Gary Marx. grants.summary: Supports nonfiction investigative reporting projects by journalists who make their living primarily as freelancers, intended for projects that demonstrate impact, breadth and significance.

grants.summary: A residential fellowship in Stuttgart for artists, researchers and cultural professionals from any discipline who are past the earliest career stage but not yet established, offering a monthly stipend plus project funding.

A narrative or documentary journalist with 2-10 years of professional experience could apply as a cultural practitioner, proposing a long-form or documentary project for the open-ended residency period, and would need to make the case in their application for why the residency suits their specific stage of development.

grants.programme: One-year fellowship for politically persecuted individuals

grants.eligibleActivity: The foundation's stated mission is protecting politically persecuted people broadly, not journalists specifically — but journalists are named as one of the recognised categories of fellows (past guests featured on the funder's page include reporters Omar Radi and Islam Shikhali), alongside artists, scientists and civil-society activists. A journalist facing political persecution can be proposed via the foundation's partner network for a year of safe housing in Hamburg while continuing their journalistic work.

amount.note: Covers housing, care and living expenses in Hamburg for one year; no specific figure stated.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of the funder's own page carried only homepage narrative (guest bios, donation appeal) with no application or eligibility detail, so this record relies on search results. Applications appear to be accepted on a rolling basis, typically via referral from partner organisations (OSCE, PEN Centre, Amnesty International, German and foreign diplomatic missions, Reporters Without Borders) rather than a direct open call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A temporary protective residency programme, typically two years, for writers, journalists and artists who face persecution because of their work and cannot continue it safely in their home country or region.

amount.note: A grant covering living costs and accommodation, plus travel expenses related to relocation; no specific figure stated. Free of charge to applicants — no application or advisory fees.

grants.notes: The funder's own page states it is currently assessing a backlog of already-received applications and is not accepting new applications; new calls will be announced on its site. Standard residency length is two years, hosted across 92 ICORN member cities in Europe and the Americas.

grants.summary: One-time emergency grants of up to $2,000 for U.S.-based professional writers — including journalists — facing a short-term financial crisis, alongside ARC's broader catalogue of emergency funding, relocation, legal and residency resources for artists and journalists at risk worldwide.

grants.summary: A new exchange programme pairing eight American and eight German journalism master's students to report jointly on transatlantic issues (trade, defence, politics, culture, the future of journalism), mentored by RIAS alumni journalists.

grants.summary: Grants for media outlets from ten Western Balkan and Visegrad countries (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czechia, Hungary, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Serbia, Slovakia) to produce audience-engaged journalism, with access to BIRN's BE-Engaged digital tool plus training, technical assistance and editorial mentoring. Eligible activities explicitly include campaigns, advocacy projects, and the production of educational and other resources and research, alongside international meetings. Applicants must be youth-led (working with people aged 15-30) and based in a Council of Europe member state.

A youth-led human-rights documentation project, media-literacy publication or reporting campaign produced with young people fits directly under this eligible-activity list, provided it is framed as non-formal education/youth participation rather than a straight commissioned news product.

amount.note: Up to €25,000 for One-off Youth Co-operation activities; up to €60,000 for International Long-term Youth Co-operation projects; Pilot Activity Grants available for smaller/rapid-response projects (amount not specified). Pilot Activity applications accepted year-round, at least 3 months before the activity starts.

grants.notes: No snapshot available (funder page returned HTTP 403). Applicant must be a youth-led NGO, informal youth collective or international youth network based in a Council of Europe member state working with people aged 15-30 — a standalone freelance journalist or conventional newsroom without a youth-led structure would not qualify on its own. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

Applications are accepted in nine languages and reviewed on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline.
grants.eligibleActivity: Front Line Defenders' own materials state that 'journalists act as human rights defenders when reporting on or investigating human rights issues,' so an at-risk freelance journalist or documenter facing threats, judicial harassment, or attack because of their reporting can apply for a Protection Grant to cover digital/physical security upgrades, legal defence fees, medical costs, or family support — safety and legal costs tied to journalistic human-rights work, not general project funding.
